raw.cause: nav handles display's MSG_ROUTE by calling MsgSend() to gps (MSG_POSITION) and is REPLY-blocked on gps. In the deadlock build, gps_handle() calls MsgSend() back to nav (MSG_HINT) before replying. nav's only thread is stuck in its own MsgSend() and never gets back to MsgReceive(), so gps stays SEND-blocked, nav stays REPLY-blocked, and display waits behind nav forever. The gps -> nav send also breaks the contract, which allows only nav -> gps.
raw.qnx_call: MsgSend from gps to nav (MSG_HINT) inside gps_handle, made before MsgReply to nav
raw.fix_summary: Remove the gps -> nav send. gps must answer MSG_POSITION using only its own state and must never send up the hierarchy to its client (blueprint allows nav -> gps only). If gps really needs hints from nav, nav should push them down in the request, for example in the text or subtype field of MSG_POSITION, or with a separate nav -> gps message. Calling back to nav is never correct.
